sources.entry: bewCloud - File sharing + sync, notes, and photos (alternative to Nextcloud and ownCloud's RSS reader). (Source Code, Clients) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: bewCloud is a self-hosted file sync, sharing, notes, and photos app built with Deno and deployed via Docker Compose.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a Deno-based web app that is run with docker compose alongside a Postgres database. It stores user-uploaded files in a local data directory and includes optional CalDAV/CardDAV contacts and calendar support through a Radicale container. Setup uses a .env file and a bewcloud.config.ts file, with a make migrate-db step to initialize or update the database. The README points to separate repositories for the desktop sync client (bewcloud-desktop) and the mobile app (bewcloud-mobile). The FAQ on the website covers private calendar and file sharing and .env-based configuration. Development commands cover starting the dev server, formatting, testing, and building production CSS.
use_cases: self-host personal file storage and sync
share files with others from my own server
host private calendar and contacts with CalDAV/CardDAV
run a private photo and notes app
how_to_run: Copy docker-compose.yml, .env.sample (save as .env), bewcloud.config.sample.ts (save as bewcloud.config.ts), and radicale-config/config into place
docker compose run --rm website bash -c "cd /app && make migrate-db"
For local development: docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up, then make migrate-db and make start
notable: Separate desktop sync client (bewcloud-desktop) and mobile app (bewcloud-mobile) repositories
Mirrored to Codeberg (Forgejo) as well as GitHub
Community NixOS and Helm chart alternatives to Docker deployment
caveats: The default configuration is described as working but very unsafe, so settings must be changed before real use
With signups disabled, the first signup still succeeds and becomes an admin
Permission issues on the data-files directory may require a chown to UID 1993 as noted in the README
